title: Q-1 assumed default: No authentication in this iteration. The endpoints are designed so an API-key dependency can be added later on the /api router without changing the contract. Recorded as a risk.
rationale: Without auth, anyone who knows a code can deactivate a link or read its stats. Per-user ownership would add a users model and change every endpoint.
alternatives: A single static API key from the API_KEY env var, sent as an X-API-Key header

title: Q-2 assumed default: 410 Gone with a JSON 'detail' key.
rationale: Affects only the redirect handler's status code and its test.

title: Q-3 assumed default: Global scope, no expiry in this iteration. A replay with the same payload returns 201 and the identical body plus 'Idempotent-Replayed: true'. A different payload returns 409.
rationale: Affects the idempotency table design and how the responses are asserted.
alternatives: Keys kept forever, global scope, replay returns the original 201 body

title: Q-4 assumed default: Not supported. Random codes only, no expiry.
rationale: Would add fields, validation and conflict handling.

title: Q-5 assumed default: Use the NFR-4 targets. Click recording is synchronous, in the same request.
rationale: Hard SLOs could require caching or async workers for click recording.
alternatives: Targets as in NFR-4 (p95 < 50 ms redirect on SQLite)

title: Q-6 assumed default: Last 30 days by default (configurable with 'days'), top 10 referrers, and total_clicks counted all-time.
rationale: Affects the stats query and its response size.
alternatives: Last 30 days and top 10 referrers, with a 'days' query parameter (1–365)

title: Q-7 assumed default: Use the socket peer address (request.client.host). Ignore X-Forwarded-For unless a future TRUSTED_PROXIES setting is added.
rationale: Affects only the value that gets hashed. Raw IPs are never stored either way.

title: ADR-1: Strict layering with services owning transactions
rationale: Routers in app/api depend only on services, schemas and core. Services accept a SQLAlchemy Session plus plain config values, use repositories, and alone call commit()/rollback(). Repositories only add/flush/query. Models import only sqlalchemy. Domain exceptions live in app/core/errors.py, which keeps services free of FastAPI imports. — Meets NFR-6, makes services unit-testable without HTTP, and puts the transaction boundaries needed for the retry/replay logic (NFR-5) in one place.
alternatives: Fat routers that call the ORM directly

title: ADR-2: Random base62 codes backed by a DB unique constraint and retry
rationale: codes.generate_code(length) uses secrets.choice over [A-Za-z0-9]. The service inserts and flushes. On IntegrityError it rolls back and retries with a new code, up to CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5). A reserved candidate (compared case-insensitively against RESERVED_CODES) uses up an attempt and is regenerated. When attempts run out the service raises a 503. — With 62^7 ≈ 3.5e12 codes collisions are rare. The DB constraint guarantees uniqueness across instances (NFR-5, NFR-9). Codes are unguessable (NFR-2, R-1).
alternatives: Hash of the URL (deterministic, enables enumeration, conflicts with the no-dedup rule)
Pre-check with SELECT before insert (racy without the constraint anyway)

title: ADR-3: Idempotency via a table with a unique key and request hash, written in the link's transaction
rationale: If the key exists: a matching request_hash replays the stored link (201, Idempotent-Replayed: true), and a different hash returns 409. Otherwise the link is inserted and flushed, then the key row is inserted and flushed in the same transaction, then the transaction commits. An IntegrityError on the key flush (a concurrent winner) rolls back both rows, after which the service re-reads the key and replays or returns 409. Keys are global and never expire (Q-3). Replays are rebuilt from the stored link row. — The DB constraint guarantees at most one link per key even with concurrent requests or several instances (FR-4, R-7). It never returns 500.
alternatives: Store the full response body JSON

title: ADR-4: App factory with a per-app engine on app.state
rationale: create_app(settings=None) builds Settings() when none are given, creates the engine and sessionmaker, and stores settings, engine and session_factory on app.state. get_db(request) and get_settings(request) read from app.state. Tables are created by Base.metadata.create_all(engine) in the lifespan startup, and the engine is disposed on shutdown. — Each test gets an isolated DB by passing Settings(database_url=tmp). There are no import-time side effects and no global mutable state (NFR-7, NFR-9).
alternatives: Module-level global engine with dependency overrides

title: ADR-5: Naive-UTC timestamps and Python-side day bucketing
rationale: All DateTime columns are portable naive DateTime values holding UTC (models.base.utcnow() = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)). Response schemas convert to tz-aware UTC on output. clicks_per_day fetches only created_at for rows in the window and groups by .date() in Python. top_referrers uses SQL GROUP BY referrer, followed by a deterministic Python sort and a cut to 10. — Avoids database-specific date functions and NULL ordering differences (R-6, FR-12), and gives identical serialization for replays.
alternatives: func.date() GROUP BY in SQL (return type differs per DB)

title: ADR-6: Raw 307 Response for redirects; ASCII-only target URLs
rationale: The redirect handler returns Response(status_code=307, headers={'Location': url, 'Cache-Control': 'no-store'}) instead of starlette's RedirectResponse, which percent-quotes the URL. URL validation additionally rejects non-ASCII characters (clients must send punycode or percent-encoded URLs). — FR-5 requires Location to equal the stored URL exactly. Response headers are latin-1 encoded, so non-ASCII would otherwise cause 500s.
alternatives: Normalize/IDNA-encode on input (violates the store-unchanged assumption)

title: ADR-7: Centralized JSON error handling with a middleware catch-all
rationale: AppError subclasses carry status_code and detail: BadRequestError 400, NotFoundError 404, ConflictError 409, GoneError 410, ServiceUnavailableError 503. Handlers are registered for AppError, StarletteHTTPException (404/405, keeping headers such as Allow), RequestValidationError (422), SQLAlchemyError (503 'Service temporarily unavailable', logged), and Exception (500). RequestLoggingMiddleware also wraps call_next in try/except: an exception is logged with its traceback and answered with 500 {"detail": "Internal Server Error"}. — Meets FR-11 and NFR-3: error bodies never contain exception text, and DB outages become 503 rather than 500.
alternatives: Relying on FastAPI defaults (the 500 is plain text)

title: ADR-8: Synchronous, best-effort click recording
rationale: After resolving an active link, the service inserts a ClickEvent and commits in its own small transaction. Any exception rolls back and is logged (logger.exception, without the IP), and the 307 is still returned. HEAD requests never record clicks. — Q-5 default: the redirect must not fail because of analytics (FR-8, R-4). HEAD is not a real visit.
alternatives: Background tasks / async queue (out of scope)
Failing the redirect when recording fails

title: ADR-9: No authentication in this iteration
rationale: The /api/links router has no auth dependency, but is structured so that a future Depends(require_api_key) can be added at router level without changing the contract. — Q-1 default; tracked as a risk.

title: ADR-10: Readiness via the shared get_db dependency
rationale: /readyz declares db: Session = Depends(get_db) and runs db.execute(text('SELECT 1')) inside try/except Exception, raising ServiceUnavailableError('Database is not ready') on failure. If an overridden get_db itself raises a SQLAlchemyError, the global SQLAlchemyError handler returns 503 too. — Tests can simulate a DB outage through app.dependency_overrides[get_db] (FR-10). No exception text is leaked.
alternatives: Probe via app.state.engine directly (overrides would not apply)

title: Execution plan: 5 packages in 3 waves
rationale: waves [['WP-1', 'WP-2', 'WP-3'], ['WP-4'], ['WP-5']]; packages in the same wave own disjoint files and run in parallel
